tone_statements.citation: Purnell, Herbert C. (ed.). 1972. Miao and Yao Linguistic Studies: Selected Articles in Chinese Translated by Chang Yü-hung and Chu Kwo-ray. Data Paper 88. Ithaca: Cornell Southeast Asia Program. Includes Li Yung-sui, Ch'en K'o-chiung & Ch'en Ch'i-kuang [李永燧、陈克炯、陈其光] 'Some problems concerning initials and tones in the Miao language' (Yuyan yanjiu 4: 65-80) and Miao Language Team 1962 'A brief description of the Miao language'.
tone_statements.quote: Pai chin has voiceless aspirated and unaspirated prenasalized obstruents. The proto voiced members of the set have been devoiced, being realized as voiceless (those occurring with tones 4 or 6 are accompanied by voiced aspiration). Thus, the Pai chin voiceless unaspirated prenasalized obstruents have two sources, the proto primary clear category and the proto muddy category. [...] Chart 14. Tones of twenty Miao linguistic areas [...] Dialect Location Tones [...] Pai chin, Hui shui, Kweichow 6 42 55 [chart continued p.110, categories 3-8:] 13 21 44 33 44 55

sources.citation: 古音小镜 kaom.net 民族语 index (hosts Chen Qiguang 2013 苗瑶语文 vocabulary database and Sun Hongkai et al. 2017 汉藏语语音和词汇 page scan).
sources.note: Checked for a hosted Central Huishui source: both hosted works cover Huishui only through 高坡 Gaopo/Jiading = Northern Huishui (nort2749); nothing for Central Huishui.

sources.citation: Wang Fushi 王辅世 (ed.). 1985. Miaoyu jianzhi 苗语简志 [A sketch of the Miao language]. Beijing: Minzu chubanshe. (archive.org scan,https://archive.org/details/20220317_20220317_1109)
sources.note: Nothing for Central Huishui. p.3 family-wide: every syllable carries a meaning-distinguishing tone; p.105 classifies 惠水次方言中部土语 (c.30,000 speakers; Huishui county seat, Baijin, parts of Changshun/Ziyun); p.139 names 甲浪 Jialang (杉木乡, Huishui) as its occasional Central-Huishui comparison point for grammar only. Phonology chapter treats Dananshan; the only 轻声 remark (p.12) concerns Layiping (Xiangxi) prefixes. Silent on stress for this variety.

sources.citation: Purnell, Herbert C. (ed.). 1972. Miao and Yao Linguistic Studies: Selected Articles in Chinese Translated by Chang Yü-hung and Chu Kwo-ray. Data Paper 88. Ithaca: Cornell Southeast Asia Program. Includes Li Yung-sui, Ch'en K'o-chiung & Ch'en Ch'i-kuang [李永燧、陈克炯、陈其光] 'Some problems concerning initials and tones in the Miao language' (Yuyan yanjiu 4: 65-80) and Miao Language Team 1962 'A brief description of the Miao language'.
sources.note: Only accessible first-hand phonological data on the Central Huishui point Pai chin (摆金 Baijin, Huishui): p.97 prenasalized obstruents (voiceless aspirated/unaspirated; tones 4 and 6 with voiced aspiration), Chart 8 p.99 forms, Chart 14 p.108 'Pai chin, Hui shui, Kweichow: 6 tones, 42 55..'. The word 'stress' does not occur anywhere in the volume; silent.

tone.says: Chart 14 ('Tones of twenty Miao linguistic areas') gives Pai chin (Baijin), Huishui: 6 tones, with the eight proto categories realised as 1=42, 2=55, 3=13, 4=21 (the Chart 8 form 'lazy' is printed 31), 5=44, 6=33, 7=44, 8=55, i.e. tones 7/5 and 8/2 merged. Section III (p.97): Baijin has voiceless aspirated and unaspirated prenasalized obstruents; proto voiced prenasalized obstruents devoiced, and syllables in tones 4 and 6 carry voiced aspiration (breathy phonation) - a tone/phonation interacti…
